title: an Animation Blueprint with a state machine and transitions
proves: author an AnimBP against a real skeleton, read the state machine back, and drive it from a pawn

steps.label: 1. find a Skeleton in the project to build against
2. find AnimSequences the state machine can play
3. build the state machine from one spec
4. read the state machine back with the independent inspector
primitive puerts_anim_blueprint_patch is NOT usable
steps.detail: NEW: not registered, and no legacy tool in the inventory covers it either
steps.why: change one state, transition or variable on an existing Animation Blueprint. puerts_anim_blueprint_build is create-only and refuses an existing asset, and lane J will not ship a patch because the UAnimBlueprintBuilderLibrary rebuild path appends instead of replacing and cannot be made failure-atomic yet. Until it exists, an animation slice is single-shot: the second prompt about the same asset has nowhere to go

steps.label: 5. attach the Animation Blueprint to a pawn's SkeletalMeshComponent
6. see the state machine blend
steps.detail: an Animation Blueprint only evaluates in a running game or in the asset editor's preview viewport. PIE is user-gated, and puerts_viewport_screenshot captures the level viewport, not an asset editor preview. The legacy anim_pose_snapshot / anim_pose_delta pair is the closest thing to a pose read-back and is behind the HTTP opt-in.

Until it exists, an animation slice is single-shot: the second prompt about the same asset has nowhere to go

proposed_schema.blocked_by: UAnimBlueprintBuilderLibrary rebuild appends rather than replaces; needs the same failure-atomic treatment BPMutatorHelpers is getting
